one_line: Typed system-design canvas that gives agents structured architecture state instead of pixels.
what_it_does: KumiDraw lets users draw and type architecture nodes and edges, refines them into typed infrastructure components, lints the graph, and exposes read_design for agent reasoning.
leverage_rationale: A typed graph materially improves agent precision over screenshot interpretation, including off-canvas nodes and edge semantics, though a general agent could still operate the editor with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly contrasts typed model access with screenshot guessing.
About text describes read_design returning nodes, boundaries, and typed calls.
Graph-backed notes and lint findings share the same state.
execution_rationale: The concept and claimed workflow are coherent, but the packet has no video or transcript and only limited visual evidence, so end-to-end completion is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo link is present but live status is unknown.
One gallery image and referenced frame sheets are listed, but visual inspection was unavailable due to system file-descriptor exhaustion.
Description specifies typed nodes, graph linting, and generated notes.
impact_rationale: Architecture teams and reviewers have a real recurring problem—diagram/document drift and unreliable AI interpretation—and the shared typed model directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies duplicated whiteboard/document workflows and AI misreading diagrams.
Lint rules target concrete architecture-review risks.
creativity_rationale: Treating architecture diagrams as a typed, compiler-like model with agent-readable semantics is a fresh and well-motivated interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Nodes refine from generic labels into typed kinds such as Cache and Redis.
Architecture linting is framed as compiler linting over the shared graph.
usability_note: Whiteboard-speed typing and automatic refinement sound approachable; graph modeling may still require learning.
red_flags: No video or transcript; demo_alive is unknown.
standouts: Strong explanation of why structured state beats visual parsing.
advance_reason: High leverage and clear audience/problem fit, despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Design canvas where agents can critique and directly manipulate UI elements through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Crit Studio provides a Figma-like canvas and tools to inspect layout, flag issues, move and resize elements, rebalance spacing, and annotate exact positions.
leverage_rationale: Structured element-level operations turn vague visual critique into precise, repeatable edits; UI-driving agents could approximate this but with substantially more ambiguity.
leverage_evidence: Tools include getCanvasState, flagIssue, moveElement, resizeElement, suggestSpacing, and annotateAt.
Description emphasizes live edits rather than chat-only suggestions.
Public repo and alive demo support a real implementation claim.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent central loop from building a mockup to critique, visible issue flags, direct edits, and conversational follow-up, with strong packaging evidence claimed.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and repository public.
Seven gallery images and three frame sheets are referenced.
About text describes a complete critique-to-edit interaction.
impact_rationale: Designers and developers have a concrete pain point in translating AI feedback into canvas changes; direct manipulation can reduce that friction materially.
impact_evidence: About text describes the cost of locating and manually fixing pixel-level feedback.
Agent can show the fix directly and respond to follow-up intent.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-active-design-editor interaction is a fresh synthesis beyond another critique chatbot and is pursued across multiple manipulation primitives.
creativity_evidence: Visible badges, exact annotations, movement, resizing, and spacing suggestions form an integrated interaction model.
Conversational correction on the same canvas is explicitly designed.
usability_note: Direct visible edits and badges should make agent actions legible and reviewable.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct video evidence in the packet.
standouts: Strong human-agent shared-state story with immediate visual feedback.
advance_reason: Best combination of meaningful WebMCP delta, coherent workflow, and credible design-tool value.

one_line: Structured collaborative document editor for humans and agents.
what_it_does: Co/Draft stores documents as blocks and exposes document state, selection, comments, and block insertion so agents can edit alongside a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured document and selection state makes agent edits more reliable than screenshot or DOM reconstruction, although document editing is a familiar agent task.
leverage_evidence: Tools named get_document_state, get_selection, add_comment, and insert_block.
Description explicitly contrasts structured state with screenshots and simulated clicks.
Shared Zustand block state is described.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused, plausible editor workflow and multiple screenshots/frame sheets, with an alive demo and public repo, but no transcript or observed run.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and repository public.
Gallery has four images and three frame sheets.
Packaging text shows adding comments, inserting a block, and resolving edits.
impact_rationale: Writers and teams regularly need collaborative editing and review; reliable agent access to selection and block structure has direct practical value.
impact_evidence: Use case centers on agents working inside a document rather than observing externally.
Comment and insertion workflow maps to common review tasks.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a familiar collaborative editor, but the shared structured human-agent document state is a meaningful interaction refinement.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits and comments are presented as part of the same document workflow.
Block model supports targeted operations.
usability_note: Simple block editing and explicit comments should be understandable to ordinary document users.
red_flags: No video or transcript; evidence is largely packaging and claims.
standouts: Clear, bounded collaboration model rather than autonomous rewriting.
advance_reason: Solid practical product with a credible structured-state advantage.

one_line: Japanese YouTube discovery service that lets agents query schedules and creator opportunities, then render picks back into the site.
what_it_does: TubeSaku organizes Japanese YouTube data and exposes tools for personalized live-stream discovery and cover-song opportunity selection.
leverage_rationale: Domain-specific structured data and returning selections into the site improve discovery precision, but a general agent could search and summarize with some friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch names agent discovery and rendering of personalized picks.
About text distinguishes site expertise in data from agent expertise in user preferences.
Demo is reported alive.
execution_rationale: The packet claims a live data product and a coherent query-select-render loop, with three gallery images and frame sheets, but no transcript or observed tool invocation.
execution_evidence: Demo_alive is alive.
Three gallery images and three frame sheets are referenced.
Description names rankings, schedules, demand signals, and historical observations.
impact_rationale: Japanese YouTube viewers and cover creators have a specific discovery problem, and personalized schedule/opportunity filtering can provide credible niche value.
impact_evidence: Use cases include finding streams at a specific time and less-crowded songs to cover.
Service organizes domain signals intended to reduce decision overload.
creativity_rationale: The site/agent division—domain evidence from the site, preference reasoning from the agent, and selections rendered back—is a fresh product framing.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly addresses the open-web problem of answers being consumed outside source sites.
Two distinct discovery modes serve viewers and creators.
usability_note: Personalized picks could simplify a data-heavy discovery experience; Japanese-language/domain specificity may narrow accessibility.
red_flags: No video or transcript; live data quality is not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Thoughtful loop that returns agent decisions and reasons to the source site.
advance_reason: Credible niche impact and a meaningful, if not transformative, WebMCP integration.

one_line: Read-only diagnostic workbench for auditing WebMCP tool contracts and agent experience.
what_it_does: WebMCP Doctor scans a public site, discovers its tools, runs deterministic AX checks, maps failure paths, compares human and agent capabilities, and proposes safer contracts without invoking target tools.
leverage_rationale: The product directly depends on structured WebMCP discovery and definitions; inspecting tool contracts is substantially more reliable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Claims seven tools audited across 42 checks in a real self-scan.
Features include contract auditing, failure X-Ray, Tool Surgeon, and human-agent parity.
Scanner explicitly never invokes target tools.
execution_rationale: The scope is unusually well specified and safety boundaries are coherent, with alive demo, public repo, and multiple evidence surfaces; still no observed video transcript.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and repository public.
Reported live self-scan with score breakdown and 100% parity.
Four gallery images and three frame sheets are referenced.
impact_rationale: WebMCP developers have a real reliability, safety, and discoverability problem; a deterministic diagnostic and repair workflow directly targets it.
impact_evidence: About text lists ambiguity, hidden tools, unsafe contracts, and poor recovery as concrete problems.
42 checks span discoverability, clarity, reliability/recovery, and safety.
creativity_rationale: The Agent Experience health-check framing and Human × Agent Digital Twin are original, memorable abstractions for a new ecosystem.
creativity_evidence: Failure X-Ray visualizes the full agent path to root cause.
Tool Surgeon compares contract quality before and after repair.
usability_note: Diagnostic dashboards may be valuable to specialists; the breadth of findings could require expert interpretation.
red_flags: Claims of a real self-scan are packet evidence, not independently observed here.
standouts: Strong safety posture: read-only scanning and explicit non-invocation boundary.
advance_reason: Directly serves the WebMCP ecosystem with a differentiated and well-scoped diagnostic product.

one_line: Human-controlled campus assistant for finding spaces, planning tasks, and executing campus actions.
what_it_does: CampusPilot exposes structured campus discovery and action tools, shows agent plans/reasoning, and requires human approval before important actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured campus actions and shared approval can improve reliability over UI driving, but the packet does not show a uniquely difficult operation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch lists discovery, availability, planning, and execution through WebMCP.
Human approval before important actions is central.
Demo is reported alive and repository public.
execution_rationale: The description is coherent but the packet has no submitted frame sheets or video, so the central workflow is not visually demonstrated and execution must be capped.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.
Demo alive and repository public.
About text lists intended workflows but provides little concrete output evidence.
impact_rationale: Students have real friction across scattered campus systems, and space discovery plus task planning is a credible everyday use case.
impact_evidence: About text identifies finding quiet study spaces and checking availability as concrete student needs.
Workflow spans discovery, planning, and controlled action.
creativity_rationale: The campus OS framing and human-in-control model are sensible, but the assistant pattern is broadly familiar.
creativity_evidence: Combines campus discovery with approval-gated agent actions.
Shows agent reasoning and planned actions in the interface.
usability_note: A single campus-oriented surface could reduce fragmented searching, assuming data integrations are complete.
red_flags: Core campus integrations and action completion are not evidenced.
standouts: Appropriate approval boundary for actions affecting students.
advance_reason: Promising concept, but the packet lacks enough execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: Approval-driven agent that fills forms and navigates confusing sites for people with disabilities.
what_it_does: BridgeAble retrofits agent assistance onto arbitrary sites, exposing explicit field semantics and letting users review and approve each step.
leverage_rationale: For high-stakes accessibility workflows, explicit typed fields and valid-value schemas can fundamentally replace unsafe visual guessing and provide a capability unavailable to many users.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts fill_field(field_id, value) with positional clicking.
Use case targets unlabeled fields and multi-step benefits forms.
Human review and approval are built into the workflow.
execution_rationale: The mission and technical rationale are compelling, but there are no frame sheets or video and the packet does not demonstrate an actual end-to-end assisted form completion.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.
Public repo and alive demo are reported.
Description is primarily rationale and claimed retrofit behavior.
impact_rationale: Disabled users navigating government and benefits sites are a specific audience facing serious consequences from errors; reliable assistance and user control could be highly valuable.
impact_evidence: About text names benefits applications, unlabeled fields, and costly submission errors.
Accessibility semantics are framed as machine-readable declarations rather than visual inference.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP as a retrofit accessibility layer for legacy sites is an ambitious and socially meaningful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly rejects redesign as the only path and proposes retrofit assistance.
Combines agent navigation with user-visible approval at every step.
usability_note: Could significantly reduce cognitive and motor burden, but arbitrary-site coverage and review ergonomics are unproven.
red_flags: No visual or video proof of the claimed arbitrary-site workflow.
Access model and real-site compatibility are unclear.
standouts: Strong alignment between structured tools and accessibility/safety needs.
advance_reason: Exceptional potential impact and WebMCP rationale justify advancement despite weak execution evidence.

one_line: Compatibility-gated smart-pet storefront that refuses purchases likely to fail in the buyer's home.
what_it_does: MintPaw records household, network, country, and cellular-plan context, evaluates five smart pet devices as okay/caution/unknown/blocked, and disables incompatible cart actions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used as a safety gate tied to shared compatibility state, not merely faster shopping; structured checks prevent a costly purchase that UI browsing makes easy.
leverage_evidence: Tools collect species, weight, household count, Wi-Fi bands, country, and cellular-plan willingness.
Blocked products cannot be added to cart and the UI reflects the same verdict.
Product copy and agent-readable records share the compatibility model.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is unusually concrete and internally consistent across agent verdicts, product page, and cart gating, with alive demo/public repo and multiple visual evidence references.
execution_evidence: Demo alive and repository public.
Six gallery images and three frame sheets are referenced.
Description gives distinct blocked versus caution behavior and supplier caveats.
impact_rationale: Cross-border smart-pet purchases have real compatibility and return-cost problems; preventing known mismatches provides direct value to shoppers and sellers.
impact_evidence: Examples include Wi-Fi bands, LTE bands, app region, plug voltage, and multi-pet fit.
Product page publishes unknown supplier information rather than hiding it.
creativity_rationale: A commerce site whose primary agent capability is refusing an incompatible sale is memorable, distinctive, and deeply integrated into checkout logic.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP is framed as a gate rather than a faster buying interface.
Caveat versus block behavior and explicit open supplier questions show nuanced pursuit.
usability_note: Compatibility verdicts and reasons should reduce buyer uncertainty, though collecting household/network details adds setup.
red_flags: No transcript; some supplier/device checks may remain unknown by design.
standouts: Excellent product-level coupling between agent decision, UI state, and cart eligibility.
advance_reason: One of the clearest examples of WebMCP changing product behavior rather than adding chat.

one_line: Synthetic ICU handoff co-pilot where agents propose risk-aware workflow changes and nurses approve them.
what_it_does: WardRound updates synthetic vitals, ranks patient risk, lets agents explain trends and draft proposals/handoff summaries, and records nurse approval or rejection in an audit trail.
leverage_rationale: Shared live state, provenance, scoped tools, and approval-gated writes make WebMCP materially safer and more reliable than generic UI automation in a high-stakes simulation.
leverage_evidence: Agent tools identify risk, explain trends, propose flags/notes/alerts/orders, and draft handoffs.
Writes become pending proposals; nurses explicitly approve or reject.
Synthetic vitals update every four seconds and decisions are audited.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a detailed coherent workflow with state updates, risk engine, proposals, approvals, and audit records, supported by frame sheets and an alive demo link, though no transcript.
execution_evidence: Description explicitly limits scope to synthetic demo data and says it is not medical software.
Three frame sheets are referenced and multiple workflow states are described.
Every clinical change has a pending/provenance/audit path.
impact_rationale: ICU handoff and triage coordination are high-value problems; even as synthetic training software, the accountable co-pilot pattern has credible educational and workflow value.
impact_evidence: Use case centers on live risk coordination and clear ownership during handover.
Human approval is mandatory for clinical workflow changes.
creativity_rationale: The agent prepares but never commits clinical actions, with provenance and nurse-controlled co-authored handoff as a deliberate interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Shared handoff is a narrow exception requiring nurse edit and explicit save.
Audit trail records both proposals and decisions.
usability_note: Risk-sorted views and explicit proposals can support busy handoffs; clinical terminology and alert density may challenge users.
red_flags: Synthetic data only; not deployable clinical software.
No transcript or direct observed agent session.
standouts: Strong safety and accountability boundaries for a high-stakes domain.
advance_reason: High-quality safety-aware agent collaboration with credible niche impact.

one_line: Shared tabletop fire-drill command room for rehearsing changing conditions with an agent and human facilitator.
what_it_does: Muster synchronizes 2D and 3D floor plans, equipment and occupant assignments, agent read/proposal tools, human confirmations, responsibility checks, and an after-action report.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared scenario state and explicit confirmation make agent planning repeatable and auditable, while generic UI driving would be error-prone across synchronized views.
leverage_evidence: Description says 2D, 3D, profiles, roster, and tool readback share authored coordinates.
Agent prepares assistance handoffs with four explicit checks but cannot assign until human confirmation.
Scenario progress and after-action decisions remain visible.
execution_rationale: The packet documents a complete rehearsal loop with scenario start/resume, 3D inspection, readback, proposal, confirmation, changing conditions, responsibility gaps, and final report approval; frame sheets and live no-login demo support the claim.
execution_evidence: Explicit no-login working loop and live URL are provided.
Three frame sheets and three gallery images are referenced.
Description details synchronized views and multiple completed workflow states.
impact_rationale: Fire-safety managers and exercise teams have a real need to rehearse ownership and changing conditions; the product provides credible training and preparedness value.
impact_evidence: Use case covers unavailable stairs, assisted occupants, ownership, and after-action review.
Human approval remains separate for assignment and final report.
creativity_rationale: Combining agentic tabletop rehearsal, synchronized 2D/3D spatial state, and human-gated responsibility assignment is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Agent answers location questions from authored equipment data.
The workflow rehearses decisions before emergencies rather than automating live response.
usability_note: Resume behavior, direct 3D inspection, and visible confirmation steps support exploration and team facilitation.
red_flags: Training simulation only, explicitly not live emergency software.
standouts: Deeply integrated spatial and procedural shared state with excellent safety boundaries.
advance_reason: Complete, ambitious, and highly differentiated use of WebMCP for accountable rehearsal.
